President Donald Trump is welcomed upon his arrival at Villamor Air Base on November 17th, 2026, in Manila, Philippines. | Photo: Getty Images	

President Donald Trump was greeted by no less than five beauty queens when he landed in the Philippines on Tuesday, according to local news outlet Rappler. As he stepped onto the tarmac, a child handed him small US and Philippine flags. A band played "YMCA," a staple at Trump rallies, as more girls in traditional bell-sleeved blouses and young men in wide-brimmed hats danced to the song.

title: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
content:
With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits.
On Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online harms. Their immediate target was Roblox, which they accused of evading legal complaints about children allegedly groomed on the platform by enforcing its own forced arbitration clause against users who agreed to the terms as minors, in some cases even under the age of 10. title: What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
content:
Building a successful company means that it can run smoothly without you. Did Jensen Huang actually build a successful company? | Image: The Verge; Getty Images; Adobe	

If the glorious AI revolution rests entirely on the well-being of one man, AI is perhaps not as robust a technology as I had previously been led to believe. Nonetheless, chunks of Silicon Valley are now insisting he is indispensable. For instance, if Elon Musk is telling the truth, then Jensen Huang (the former CEO of Nvidia, a company with a market cap of about $3 trillion) has been making deals that were "a handshake with Jensen" with suppliers - "not a written contract," Musk wrote.

title: Disney’s new Star Wars animatronics interact with guests using AI
content:
As advanced and lifelike as the animatronic characters at Disney parks have become, they typically either stick to predefined movements and routines, or there's an out of sight puppeteer helping make their behavior appear more spontaneous. That could soon change as Walt Disney Imagineering R&D has revealed three new Audio-Animatronic prototypes that rely on Amazon's AWS cloud and AI capabilities to respond in unique ways to guest interactions in real-time.
The three animatronics, named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre'a, and Jibu Bre'a, are based on the Star Wars alien characters called the Anzellans that were featured in The Mandalorian and Grogu film  …

title: Remember the frontier AI pause? Chip companies don’t either
content:
Nvidia began shipping its most advanced AI computing system, the Vera Rubin NVL72, calling it the “fastest product ramp in the company’s history.” | Image: Nvidia	

This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing advances in the most powerful AI models, warning that they could be used to launch cyberattacks or become harder for their own creators to control.

title: Will Wright’s next game uses AI to map your memories
content:
Will Wright, the creator of legendary franchises like SimCity and The Sims, is working on a new game - and it's built around AI. The new title, focused on your memories, is called MyMems. Like Wright's other titles, it sounds extremely ambitious, giving players a new way to explore worlds they create on their own. "We want to take your autobiography and turn it into a toy world," he tells The Verge.
The MyMems website describes the mobile game as a "social simulation" with worlds "built from your memories and the people who shaped you." You can add "memories" to your game, like speaking a short story to your phone, and those memories are ge …

title: Nvidia isn’t selling any more AI chips to China
content:
Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China despite the approval it received from the White House to do so in December last year. The announcement was made by interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress during an earnings call on Tuesday, marking a notable shift for the company that, under former CEO Jensen Huang, fought for the right to ship its powerful Hopper architecture H200 chips to China.
"Our guidance ⁠does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping ​licenced Hopper data center products to China," Kress said. She did not explain why Nvidia was ceasing its H200 processor shipments or  …

title: Suno now lets you make AI videos for your AI music
content:
Here are some of the examples that Suno provided to show what Visuals is capable of. | Image: Suno	

Suno has introduced image and video generation in its latest effort to expand beyond being an AI music platform. The new feature, called "Visuals," allows users to turn Suno songs into AI-generated video clips that automatically lipsync to lyrics, or make images via prompt descriptions that can be used as thumbnails and album artwork.
Visuals is available on web, iOS, and Android. The exact layout differs across Suno's desktop and mobile interfaces, but users will find a new Visuals tab under Create mode on each version. title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella onstage at Microsoft Ignite. | Image: Microsoft / YouTube	

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he's AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. "I am AGI-pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy's organization around AGI?" he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco.
